messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected - inference-prod API 5xx rate spike. 5m error rate = 18% (>SLO). Root: /v1/generate - elevated CPU on gpu-pool-a. Paging maya (oncall).

maya: ack @Incident Bot - looking. pulling logs and recent deploys.

alex: I saw a config push 30m ago to autoscaler rules for gpu-pool-a. Maya can you confirm if nodes spun up?

maya: checking k8s. `kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=gpu-pool-a` returns CrashLoopBackOff on 4/12 replicas. logs show OOM when loading model shard.

sre-lead: :loud_sound: tagging vendors - need AWS node health and EBS perf checks. @aws-support can you confirm if there's noisy neighbor / instance host issues in us-west-2c?

aws-support: thanks for the ping. Opening case now. Please share instance ids and timestamps; assign case ID 7893421. We're looking into host-level metrics.

alex: instance ids: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h (gpu-1), i-0h7g6f5e4d3c2b1a (gpu-2). Error window 1753006700-1753007000 UTC. Sending to AWS support with logs.

maya: temp mitigation: scaling down model to smaller variant and restarting pods to avoid OOM. Rolling restart command:
```
kubectl set image deploy/inference-backend inference-backend=redwood/inference:canary-smaller
kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-backend -n inference
```

sam: Preparing customer-facing note. Draft for status page / email:
Status page blurb (draft): "We are investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting text generation in us-west-2. Engineers are performing a rollback and mitigations. Some requests may fail or be slower than usual. We will provide updates every 15 minutes."

sam: Customer email draft:
"Hi — we're currently investigating an issue causing failed text generation requests for some customers in the US-WEST region. Our engineering team is actively mitigating; you may see increased errors or timeouts. We will update you within 30 minutes or sooner with more details. Sorry for the disruption — Redwood Inference Support"

sre-lead: Internal comms template (use this for incident channel and exec):
"INCIDENT (inference-prod - us-west-2)
Severity: S2
Impact: 15-20% 5xx rate on /v1/generate, region us-west-2
Mitigation in progress: rolling model to smaller variant; restarting pods; vendor escalated (AWS case 7893421)
Next update: +15m
Owner: maya (oncall), escalation: alex (infra)"

alex: AWS response: seeing host-level CPU steal spikes on gpu-1. They've scheduled host isolation and moved instance to new host; ETA for host migration ~22 minutes. Asking us to drain i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h now.

maya: starting cordon/drain for gpu-1 and gpu-2:
```
kubectl drain ip-10-0-1-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference
```

ops-bot: :gear: Runbook step: drain instance -> evict pods -> nodes should rebuilt. If evictions stuck >10m, escalate to SRE lead.

jamie: evictions proceeding, pods restarting on other nodes. 5xx rate dropping to 4% over last 3m.

sam: updating status page: "Mitigation started; error rate decreasing. Some customers may still see errors. Next update in 15 minutes." publishing now.

aws-support: Host migration in progress, we will confirm when instance health checks are green. Case 7893421 — escalation to NOC in progress.

maya: switching primary owner to alex for follow-through on vendor comms and node rebuild. Handoff note: I'm staying until things are stable. alex, you own post-mitigation RCA and customer root cause.

alex: ack. I'll keep AWS case open and get the host health report. Planning to roll back autoscaler rule change if correlated. Capturing timeline for RCA.

sre-lead: good. please capture exact deploys and config diff. Also save the error traces sample for quality team.

sam: customer notification updated and queued for impacted customers with reply-to support@redwood.ai. Monitoring for replies.

maya: final check — error rate steady at 0.9% for 10m, latency back to baseline. Marking incident as recovering.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status changed to Recovering. Please file postmortem and reference AWS case 7893421.

alex: resolution summary (to include in postmortem): "Root cause: OOMs from model shard load compounded by host-level CPU steal on AWS host. Immediate mitigations: rolled to smaller model variant, drained affected hosts, AWS host migration. Long-term actions: revert risky autoscaler change, add node health gating to rollout, add model shard prefetch memory guardrails."

sam: sending closure email to impacted customers with note + link to status page update.

jamie: leaving oncall notes in pagerduty and handoff to next oncall (leo) in 10m.

maya: closing out for now. Thanks everyone. :pray:
